title: The Problem of Time in Quantum Cosmology
bottleneck: Canonical quantum gravity yields a timeless Wheeler-DeWitt equation, with no agreed way to recover the flowing time of cosmology from it. Relational-time proposals, unimodular gravity, and emergent-time scenarios each solve part of the problem while raising new ones, and none yields distinct cosmological predictions. Without a satisfactory account of time, quantum cosmology cannot describe the evolution it was built to explain.
why_it_blocks: A quantum theory of the universe that cannot describe cosmic time cannot describe cosmic history. It also blocks a complete account of the universe's origin, which is cosmology's central narrative.
current_state: The problem is conceptual rather than experimental; it persists as the central interpretational obstacle in quantum cosmology. The problem is widely seen as a clue that our formulation of quantum gravity is incomplete.
